summary:
Gibraltar is a self-governing territory with its own legislature and Supreme Court, which enact and interpret its civil and criminal law. Statutes of the United Kingdom do not apply here of their own force. The United Kingdom's Equality Act 2010 and the single-sex-services code issued in 2025 reach Gibraltar only if extended by Order in Council, and no such extension appears in the sourced material.

No legal process exists in Gibraltar to change the gender recorded on a person's documents. A trans visitor therefore travels under a marker that no local authority can amend, and can expect to be identified publicly under it wherever papers are produced, including at the border.

Discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation and gender reassignment has been prohibited by legislation in force since 2007. The sourced material does not state how far that protection reaches in practice: whether it covers access to services, accommodation, healthcare or shared facilities, and how a complaint is pursued.

Identity-based violence has a statutory footing. Parliament amended the Crimes Act 2011 on 19 September 2013 to criminalise hatred and harassment on grounds of sexual orientation; the amendment received royal assent on 25 September and came into force on 10 October 2013. In July 2026 Parliament passed a bill extending hate crime and hate speech protection to transgender identity. A trans visitor therefore has a named offence to invoke in respect of conduct targeting gender identity, distinct from the older sexual-orientation offence.

A second bill passed in July 2026 makes it an offence to offer or practise conversion therapy. The sourced material gives the date of passage but no commencement date and no account of any exemptions.

Partnership recognition is settled. Civil partnerships have been available since 2014, and same-sex marriage since December 2016, when the bill passed unanimously. The legislative process ran through a public consultation in December 2015 that left opinion divided, an inter-ministerial committee weighing submissions, and support from the main parties.
tangentialFactors:
Official response to hostility has been public and prompt. Following an incident of anti-gay abuse in July 2021, the Ministry for Justice and Equality said it would urgently consider legislation against what the Chief Minister, Fabian Picardo, described as disgusting lurking homophobia circulating on social media during Pride month; a proposal to make denigration of a person on grounds of sexual orientation a specific criminal offence was under examination at that time.

The wider record points one way. The House of Commons Foreign Affairs Committee's 2008 inquiry into overseas territories recommended that discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender status be made illegal across all such territories, and its 2007-08 reporting set accountability and good-governance expectations for territories including Gibraltar. Gibraltar's own legislation has since delivered that protection for sexual orientation, and from July 2026 for transgender identity as well.

Equal treatment under criminal law arrived in stages rather than at once. The Supreme Court ruled on 8 April 2011 that the age of 18 for gay sex was unconstitutional; the gender-neutral Crimes Act 2011, approved in August 2011, set a uniform age of consent of 16 with effect from 23 November 2012. Before that gay male minors faced 18, and a private member's bill to equalise the age was defeated in Parliament on 18 May 2009.
localsOnly:
Family law has been substantially rewritten for residents. On 10 April 2013 the Supreme Court held section 5(2) of the Adoption Act 1951 contrary to the Gibraltar Constitution, on a challenge by a long-term lesbian couple refused adoption for want of legal recognition of their relationship; Parliament then amended the law through the 2014 civil partnership legislation. The Adoption Act 2023 took full effect on 18 April 2024 and expressly allows same-sex couples to adopt without discrimination.

Reproductive provision follows the same direction. In February 2021 Gibraltar enacted a surrogacy law permitting non-commercial altruistic surrogacy for married couples or civil partners unable to conceive, with automatic recognition of children of same-sex couples conceived through artificial insemination. In June 2017 the Gibraltar Health Authority approved an amendment to its in vitro fertilisation policy allowing lesbian couples to access assisted reproductive technology. Same-sex activity has been legal since 1993.
outOfScopeNotes:
Unresolved: how the 2007 protection against discrimination on grounds of gender reassignment operates in practice. The statute is sourced, but no complaint, ruling or enforcement action under it appears in the material.

Unresolved: commencement and scope of the two bills passed in July 2026, covering transgender identity in hate-crime and hate-speech law and the ban on conversion therapy. Passage is sourced; assent, effective dates and any drafting of exemptions are not.

Unresolved: whether an Order in Council has ever extended the United Kingdom's Equality Act 2010 or its 2025 single-sex-services code to Gibraltar. The sourced material records no such extension, which is not the same as a confirmed decision not to extend.

Not sourced: any gender-recognition bill introduced to Gibraltar's Parliament even unsuccessfully, and any policy of the Gibraltar Health Authority concerning trans patients or gender-affirming care.
